rv.q: If I say that Irish Theatre of Chicago's new production of Brian Friel's Molly Sweeney is an absolutely beautiful one, someone is going to wonder what the heck I'm talking about.
This is a magnificent production by the celebrated Irish playwright, Brian Friel, produced after a long absence by the much-admired and celebrated Irish Theatre of Chicago.

The key theme threading through all their stories, which comes through with clean and sorrowful precision in Siiri Scott’s staging for Irish Theatre of Chicago, is that seeing someone clearly requires far more than ophthalmic intervention.
I will not tell you more except to let you know that this is storytelling at its finest and even with the Irish brogues ( which were very well done) the dialogue was understandable.
The acting was incredible and the Irish accents were spot on.

cn.t: Friel's meditation on sight and understanding earns strong praise for its haunting exploration of a blind woman's failed vision restoration. Critics laud the metaphysical depth and beautiful staging, though the monologue format proves challenging.
